# SEC filing-index ingestion on Azure — Roadmap

> For agentic workers: REQUIRED SKILL: derive-roadmap — resume via its
> reconcile step; route each unticked stage per its ROUTING line; never plan
> this document wholesale.

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md (outcomes ranked by the project owner, 2026-11-06, in list order). Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace with four member packages (root `pyproject.toml`). Azure platform per the ADR, which is still Proposed (spec §7 step 1).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A historical filing-index baseline built from archived quarterly indexes over a chosen range | R1, §2.1, §4.2 | A | 1 | Up to about 135 quarterly indexes if the range runs from 1993 Q1 to 2026 Q3. That is under a minute of requests at 3 req/s. Bytes and time per quarter are measured by Stage 1. |
| O2 | The catalog kept current from daily indexes, catching up after missed runs | R2, §4.2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily indexes a year, one request each plus listings; negligible against the budget (§4.3) |
| O3 | Downloaded indexes parsed, validated and published as one canonical Parquet filing-index dataset | R3, §4.5, §4.6 | A | 3 | Measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The pipeline running on Azure: ADF triggers, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS files, Table Storage state, Monitor logs | R4, §4.1, §4.9 | A | 4 | No dollar estimate is possible before deployment; measured by Stage 6 |
| O5 | Backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation using one downloader, parser and publisher | R5, §4.1 | A | 5 | No material cost |
| O6 | Stored source bytes reprocessed after a parser change without downloading again | R6, §4.3, §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage for every retained snapshot; volume measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | Quarterly indexes re-read on a schedule, with later SEC changes reflected in the catalog | R7, §4.2, §4.4 | A | 7 | One request per supported quarter per week (about 135 at the full range, §4.8). Re-transform runs only on changed hashes. |
| O8 | All SEC traffic held to one shared request budget, however many workers run | R8, §4.3 | A | 8 | Throughput is capped at 3 req/s against the SEC's 10 req/s ceiling (§4.3) |
| O9 | Readers find each quarter's current data through one versioned pointer, never partial files | R9, §4.5, §4.6 | A | 9 | No material cost |
| O10 | No record leaves the catalog without approval tied to the exact source snapshot | R10, §4.4 | A | 10 | Owner time per gated closed-quarter withdrawal; frequency measured by Stage 5 |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and the rate target held as reviewed, validated configuration | R11, §4.8, §5 | A | 11 | No material cost |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Open questions

- Spec §4.9 places all code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The repository also holds `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-index-ingest` scaffolds. The root script `sec-edgar = "sec_edgar:main"` points at a module that does not exist. Stage 1's brainstorming settles which package owns what and records the answer in its Handoff.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter and one real daily index, end to end
      Objective: Download one archived quarterly master index and one published daily master index, then parse and validate them and write the canonical rows as Parquet, all run locally on real SEC data.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: an SEC User-Agent identity from the project owner (§4.8 `sec.user_agent`); the empty package scaffolds
      Produces: a shared downloader (identifying User-Agent, 3 req/s, no bursts), content-addressed raw snapshots with SHA-256, and a parser to the `sec-index-v1` row contract (§4.5); the package split settled (Open questions); specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O3, a Parquet output for the chosen quarter and daily index whose every row meets the §4.5 row contract, with malformed rows refused per §4.6. Measured cost of the real run (byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory, request count and observed rate) is recorded in the findings file.
      Leaves out: versioned generations and the active pointer (Stage 2); the source manifest, checkpoints and resume (Stage 3); replay from raw (Stage 3); the shared lease budget (Stage 6); Azure deployment (Stage 6); full configuration validation, alerts and scheduling (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as an immutable generation with a manifest and change report behind one conditionally updated active pointer, using a local stand-in for the Table Storage pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 1's parser and Parquet output (plan <id>, Handoff)
      Produces: generation-addressed curated paths, a publication manifest and a conditional active pointer per quarter (§4.5, §4.6); the crash-injection tests for publication (§6 Publication)
      Exit: O9, readers resolve a quarter only through its pointer. Crashes injected before the files finish, before the pointer update and right after it leave only complete generations readable.
      Leaves out: the withdrawal gate (Stage 5); Table Storage itself (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Backfill over a range, with replay
      Objective: Ingest a configured inclusive quarter range with per-source checkpoints, and reprocess stored bytes after a parser change with SEC access disabled.
      Outcomes: O1, O6
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader and parser; Stage 2's publication path
      Produces: the source, snapshot, processing and attempt manifest records (§4.5); golden fixtures for every historical format in the chosen range (§4.6); a backfill run report of complete, pending and failed units (§4.2); specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: O1, every quarter in the chosen range is published, or its gap is listed in the run report, and an interrupted run resumes without redoing finished units. O6, a parser-version bump rebuilds output from raw storage with zero SEC requests and no duplicate logical records. The findings file records the measured cost of the real range run.
      Leaves out: daily sources (Stage 4); reconciliation (Stage 5); the shared lease (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes from the handoff date, catching up across missed runs and quarter boundaries, with overlap against the baseline deduplicated.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 3's manifest and backfill baseline
      Produces: daily discovery from `index.json` listings with a discovery boundary that never advances past a failed read (§4.2); open-quarter precedence (§4.4)
      Exit: O2, a run after a simulated multi-quarter outage publishes every listed daily index it missed, reports `no_new_sources` on an empty valid listing, and keeps older pending sources discoverable.
      Leaves out: closed-quarter reconciliation and withdrawals (Stage 5); the trigger schedule (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation and the withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read every supported quarterly index, publish safe additions and field updates, and hold any closed-quarter key removal for hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10, O5
      Consumes: Stages 2–4
      Produces: reconciliation runs, change reports and withdrawal approval records (§4.4, §4.5)
      Exit: O7, a changed quarterly snapshot publishes a new generation whose change report names the additions and updates, and an unchanged hash skips transformation. O10, a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval names its exact hash and generation, and stale daily replay cannot resurrect an excluded key. O5, backfill, daily and reconciliation runs call the same downloader, parser and publisher and differ only in source selection.
      Leaves out: the Azure approval store and alerts (Stages 6, 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Azure platform and the shared request budget
      Objective: Run the shared commands as Container Apps Jobs orchestrated by ADF, with ADLS and Table Storage in place of the local stand-ins, and every collector behind one Storage-backed lease.
      Outcomes: O4, O8
      Consumes: acceptance of the ADR and spec (§7 step 1); Stages 1–5
      Produces: versioned infrastructure, managed identities, job and pipeline definitions with triggers disabled (§4.9); the `discover`, `collect`, `transform` and `publish` CLI exchanging worksets (§4.1); the shared lease (§4.3)
      Exit: O4, in an isolated environment, an ADF run starts and polls a job to a terminal state, requires the matching worker result file, and stops on an ambiguous start without relaunching. O8, concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors never overlap as request issuers, including across lease loss and takeover. The bounded live smoke test (§7 step 4) records its measured cost, Azure spend included.
      Leaves out: alerts, runbooks, schedules and trigger enablement (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Configuration, observability and scheduled operation
      Objective: Validate all configuration before I/O, add alerts and runbooks, enable the triggers, and accept scheduled operation from observed runs.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 6's deployed environment
      Produces: typed configuration (`conf/sec-edgar-ingest.yaml`) with §5 configuration refusals; alerts and reports per §4.7; runbooks (§8); a release record (§7 Exit)
      Exit: O11, each §5 configuration error is refused before any network request. The backfill, the daily catch-up and one manual reconciliation complete per §7 steps 6–8. The next scheduled runs are checked against their durable reports.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, and writing-plans copies it verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric (derive-roadmap §6) over O1–O11. Then run it over each numbered spec requirement that no outcome's `Spec` cell cites; R1–R11 are all cited. A requirement counts as met only on a path:line or test-name piece of evidence that names its implementing stage plan. Each unmet outcome becomes a new stage or a written deferral.

---

Here is the roadmap draft for `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`. It has seven stages, and their order diverges from your ranking because of dependencies: quarter publication (O9) must exist before the backfill writes quarters, and Azure and the shared lease (O4, O8) wait until the pipeline works locally on real data. Do you approve this partition, including Stage 1 settling which of the four scaffold packages owns the code, so I can commit it on `main` and hand off Stage 1?
